::: {#exr-duck-see-magnet}
The rate of energy while running captured the "amount of running" in units of mile-pounds. But doesn't speed enter into it? It's common sense that running faster involves a larger "amount of running." If this were the case, the units for the amount of running would be mile-pounds-mile/hour or miles^2^-pound/hour. That's a strange-looking unit. It turns out, however, that running speed is not an important factor in determining the amount of energy used to run a mile-pound. Instead, the increased effort for running fast is due to higher *power* use, where power is energy per time. 
:::
